language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Good Evening! I am Captain John Morrow. I was just checking the weather for tomorrow. You know what they say: "Red sky at night, sailor's delight. Red sky in the morning, sailor's warning."
If the sunset is nice and red, it should be nice out tomorrow. If it is red in the morning, then we're in for bad weather. That's the theory anyway.

There is a lot you can learn from the sky. There is so much going on out there in outer space. What do you know about this universe we live in? Maybe I can share my knowledge with you! I like to think of myself as quite the astronomer!
An astronomer is someone who studies the parts of the universe including stars, planets, and moons.

Sailors, like myself, can use stars to navigate at night. Stars rotate through the night sky and their position can help us know where we are in relation to the stars.
In the past, people have looked up at the stars and identified patterns. These patterns are called constellations. Being able to recognize a constellation in the sky can be a lot of fun!
Let's identify some constellations together.

activities.subtitle: This constellation is called the Big Dipper in North America, the Plough in the United Kingdom and Saptarshi in India. Other countries have other names for it too. Do you see it?

Let's take a look at the planets now. We live in a solar system. The centre of our solar system is a star, the sun.
The solar system is made up of all the objects that orbit the sun. In our solar system, we have eight planets that orbit the sun.
Each planet is different. See what you know about them.

You've learned a lot about outer space, now let's try and put these pieces together! You know we live in a solar system with a Sun and planets.

But there are millions of other solar systems in the universe. Each star you see is a Sun with its own planets! Our universe is actually made up of billions of galaxies and each contains billions of stars and solar systems!
Now that you have learned about the universe, let's do a little review. See what all you remember.
